title_en: Interim Regulations on Prohibition of Arbitrary Levies on Enterprises

articles.content_en: These Regulations are formulated for the purpose of prohibiting the imposition of apportionments on enterprises and protecting the lawful rights and interests of enterprises.

For the purposes of these Regulations, "apportionment" means any act of requiring an enterprise to provide financial resources, materials, or manpower in any manner, beyond the provisions of laws and regulations.

No state organ, people's organization, military unit, enterprise, public institution, or any other social organization (hereinafter collectively referred to as "units") shall impose apportionments on enterprises.
For fee collection items provided for by laws and regulations, no unit shall exceed the scope of collection, raise the standards of collection, or alter the methods of collection.

No unit shall compel an enterprise to sponsor, subsidize, or donate money or property.
The funds voluntarily sponsored, subsidized, or donated by an enterprise shall be disbursed only from its own funds and shall not be included in costs.
Except as provided for by laws and regulations, no unit shall compel an enterprise to purchase marketable securities or to raise funds from the enterprise in any other form.
Except for compulsory insurance items provided for by laws and regulations, no unit shall compel an enterprise to take out insurance.
Except as provided for by laws and regulations, no unit shall convert voluntary public welfare labor into apportionment of money or property on enterprises.
No unit shall impose other forms of apportionments on enterprises in violation of these Regulations.

It is prohibited to retaliate against enterprises that resist apportionments.
No unit shall use its authority or business convenience to give discriminatory treatment to enterprises that resist apportionments.

Where, in the event of an emergency such as a natural disaster or accident, local people's governments at various levels make a decision requiring an enterprise to provide financial resources, materials, or manpower, such action shall not be deemed as an apportionment, but the matter shall be reported to the people's government at the next higher level for recordation afterwards.

An enterprise shall have the right to refuse any unit's apportionment.
Where an enterprise is unclear as to the nature of a fee collection item, it shall report to the finance department of the people's government at the level above the fee-collecting unit, and may only make payment after it is verified that the item is in conformity with laws and regulations.

The finance department shall, within thirty days of receiving the report submitted by the enterprise in accordance with the second paragraph of Article 13, make a reply as to whether the fee shall be paid. Failure to reply within the time limit shall be deemed as disagreement with the payment.
Where an enterprise has any objection to the reply of the finance department, it may report to the finance department at the next higher level.
Any unit or individual shall have the right to accuse, report, or expose acts of apportionment to the audit authority or other relevant departments.

The audit authority may, together with the relevant departments, investigate cases of apportionment that it receives through accusations, reports, exposures, or that are transferred by other departments in accordance with Article 17. The unit under investigation must truthfully provide information and shall not create difficulties or obstruct the investigation.

The planning, finance, price, taxation, banking, and other departments shall strengthen supervision and inspection. Where they discover any act of apportionment, they shall promptly stop it; if the stop is ineffective, they shall transfer the case to the audit authority for case-filing and handling.

Where an act is confirmed by the audit authority as an apportionment, the audit authority shall notify the unit that imposed the apportionment to cease the act and return the apportioned money or property within a specified time limit; if the unit fails to return it within the time limit, the audit authority may notify the bank with which the unit has an account to deduct and repay the amount from its relevant deposits.
Where the apportioned money or property no longer exists and cannot be recovered, the audit authority may notify the relevant department to deduct and confiscate an amount equivalent to the value of the apportioned money or property, or take other economic compensation measures.

The supervisory authority or the relevant competent department may, depending on the severity of the circumstances, impose corresponding administrative sanctions on the person in charge and the persons directly responsible of the unit that imposed the apportionment.

Anyone who, in violation of these Regulations, retaliates against a unit or individual that has accused, reported, exposed, or resisted an apportionment shall be given a severe punishment; if a crime is constituted, the judicial authority shall investigate criminal liability according to law.

Where persons misappropriate or share the apportioned money or property, the supervisory authority shall investigate the administrative liability of the person in charge of the unit; if a crime is constituted, the judicial authority shall investigate criminal liability according to law.
The audit authority may commend persons who have rendered meritorious service in reporting, exposing, or resisting apportionments.

The recovered apportioned money or property shall, if the enterprise has reported or accused the matter, be returned to the enterprise; if no report or accusation has been made, it shall all be turned over to the central finance.

Where the unit that imposed the apportionment disagrees with the decision on economic penalty made by the audit authority, it may, within fifteen days of receipt of the decision, apply to the audit authority at the next higher level for review. The execution of the original penalty decision shall not be suspended during the period of review.
For the purposes of these Regulations, "enterprise" means an enterprise registered with the administrative authority for industry and commerce according to law.

The imposition of apportionments on state organs, people's organizations, military units, public institutions, and other social organizations (including capital construction units) and individuals shall be handled by reference to these Regulations.
These Regulations shall come into force as of May 20, 1988.
